entries.title: Tiny magnetic waves could unlock quantum computers the size of a penny
entries.description: A major breakthrough in quantum technology has turned magnons, tiny magnetic waves once considered too short-lived for practical use, into promising carriers of quantum information. Researchers extended their lifetime by nearly 100 times, reaching up to 18 microseconds, and discovered that the main limitation is not a law of physics but the purity of the material itself. That means future improvements could come from better manufacturing rather than entirely new discoveries.

entries.title: Scientists create quantum sound device that could transform communications
entries.description: A new quantum device can generate precisely controlled bursts of sound-like particles, or phonons, by forcing electrons through an ultra-thin crystal at extremely low temperatures. The surprising behavior pushes beyond the limits predicted by current theories, suggesting scientists need to rethink how energy moves through advanced materials. In the future, the breakthrough could lead to phonon lasers, faster communications, improved medical technologies, and powerful new sensing systems.

entries.title: ADB Approves $182.89 Million Loan to Strengthen Public School System in Karnataka, India
entries.description: ADB has approved a $182.89 million (in yen equivalent) loan to help India strengthen the public school system in Karnataka, expanding access to high-quality learning and improving academic performance for more than a million students, including female and disadvantaged learners.

entries.title: ADB Approves $230 Million Loan to Modernize Water Supply and Sanitation in Chennai, India
entries.description: ADB has approved a $230 million loan to modernize and expand Chennai’s water supply and sanitation infrastructure, benefiting 4.5 million residents in the Greater Chennai area.

entries.title: ADB Approves $70 Million Loan to Support Fiscal and Governance Reforms in the Kyrgyz Republic
entries.description: ADB has approved a $70 million concessional loan for subprogram 2 of the Sustainable Fiscal Management and Governance Improvement Program, supporting policy reforms to strengthen fiscal resilience, transparency, and public resource management in the Kyrgyz Republic.

entries.title: ADB Approves $50 Million Loan to Modernize Nepal’s Customs, Boost Trade and Jobs
entries.description: ADB has approved a $50 million policy-based loan to help Nepal modernize its customs administration, boost trade, and support job creation.

entries.title: ADB Approves $200 Million Emergency Assistance for Sri Lanka’s Post-Cyclone Ditwah Recovery
entries.description: ADB has approved a $200 million emergency assistance package for Sri Lanka’s recovery and reconstruction following Cyclone Ditwah.

entries.title: ADB Approves $11 Million Grant to Boost Health Services In Kiribati
entries.description: ADB has approved an $11 million grant for health initiatives in Kiribati, highlighting the critical role the Asian Development Fund plays in supporting the country’s development priorities.

entries.title: ADB Approves $13 Million Financing for Resilient Urban Development in Bhutan
entries.description: ADB has approved a $13 million financing package to help the Government of Bhutan strengthen resilient urban infrastructure and expand affordable rental housing for low-income and vulnerable households, particularly in Thimphu and Phuentsholing.

entries.title: ADB Establishes North Pacific Subregional Office, Expanding Support in Region
entries.description: ADB announced the establishment of a subregional office to support its expanding operations in the North Pacific, strengthening the bank’s commitment to its Pacific developing member countries as a steadfast partner for growth, development, and resilience.

entries.title: ADB, Golomt Bank Partner to Expand Sustainable and Inclusive Finance in Mongolia
entries.description: ADB and Golomt Bank Joint Stock Company (Golomt Bank) have signed a $64 million loan agreement to support sustainable finance and expand lending to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including women-owned businesses in Mongolia.

entries.title: ADB Approves Additional Financing to Strengthen Resilient Coffee Livelihoods in Timor-Leste
entries.description: ADB has approved $4.95 million in additional financing for the Coffee and Agroforestry Livelihood Improvement Project in Timor-Leste, helping smallholder farmers adopt sustainable coffee-based agroforestry practices that improve coffee production and food security.

entries.title: ADB, Converse Bank Sign $15 Million Financing to Boost Women-Owned MSMEs and Sustainable Lending in Armenia
entries.description: ADB has signed a financing package of up to $15 million with Converse Bank Closed Joint Stock Company to expand access to finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and households, and to support sustainable lending in Armenia.

entries.title: ADB Approves $42.2 Million Loan to Boost Bamboo Industry in India's Northeast Region
entries.description: ADB has approved a $42.2 million small expenditure financing facility to develop the bamboo industry in India’s northeastern states, boosting agricultural productivity, strengthening rural livelihoods, and reducing dependence on imports.

entries.title: ADB President Taps Global Business Leaders to Take on Asia and the Pacific’s Toughest Challenges
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda brought together some of the world’s most influential business leaders to put private sector muscle behind solutions to Asia and the Pacific’s most pressing problems.

entries.title: ADB Begins Voting Process for President; Masato Kanda Nominated
entries.description: ADB has opened the voting process for its President for a 5-year term beginning on 24 November 2026.

entries.title: ADB President Meets German President; Calls for Faster Global Action to Mobilize Investment at Hamburg Sustainability Conference
entries.description: ADB President Masato Kanda met with Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier at the Hamburg Sustainability Conference to express support for Germany’s investments in multilateralism and global development.

entries.title: ADB Backs Major Public Spending Reforms in the Philippines
entries.description: The Philippines has endorsed a government-wide plan, backed by ADB, to reform how public money is allocated, spent, and accounted for, with the aim of delivering better services for the Filipino people.

entries.title: ADB Issues Inaugural Digital Solutions Bond to Open New Growth Pathways
entries.description: ADB has issued its first digital solutions theme bond to finance a pool of eligible projects supporting digital connectivity across Asia and the Pacific.

entries.title: How might AI transform science?
entries.description: Nobel Prize laureates Demis Hassabis and Paul Nurse join Alison Noble, Chair of the Royal Society Science in the Age of AI Working Group, to discuss how scientists can harness AI tools, and what challenges it might bring about. entries.description: The European Space Agency has contracted Spanish company EMXYS for the first CubeSat designed to operate on the surface of an asteroid. Don Quijote is a shoebox-sized spacecraft that will be deployed onto the Apophis asteroid by ESA’s Ramses mission before the asteroid flies by Earth on 13 April 2029.

entries.description: Building on the remarkable success of the Earth Explorer Aeolus wind mission, the European Space Agency has given Airbus Defence and Space in the UK the authorisation to proceed to begin the development of Aeolus’ successor, Aeolus-2 – which is set to be built to enhance operational weather forecasts.

entries.title: XMM-Newton helps revise distance to outer spiral arms
entries.description: The European Space Agency’s XMM-Newton and NASA’s Chandra X-ray space telescopes have spotted the aftermath of three bright explosions echoing through the outer spiral arms of our galaxy, the Milky Way. By measuring the distance to these echoes, they find the outer arms to be up to 10% further away than we thought.

entries.title: A strange LIGO signal could reveal the missing link behind dark matter
entries.description: An unusual gravitational wave signal has renewed hopes that primordial black holes, long considered purely theoretical, may finally be within reach of discovery. If confirmed, they could solve one of astronomy's greatest mysteries by explaining the nature of dark matter.

entries.title: Scientists make quantum time flow backward in stunning physics breakthrough
entries.description: Researchers have created quantum control techniques that can make a system appear to run backward in time. By precisely managing quantum measurements, they can reshape the system's arrow of time and even harvest energy from the measurement process itself. The breakthrough could lead to more powerful quantum computers, quantum batteries, and other advanced technologies.

entries.title: Millions of exploding stars could soon reveal dark energy's secrets
entries.description: A new AI-powered framework could transform how astronomers measure the expansion of the Universe. By analyzing images of Type Ia supernovae and modeling their environments in unprecedented detail, researchers can estimate cosmic distances with near-spectroscopic accuracy. The technique is designed for the flood of data expected from the upcoming Vera C. Rubin Observatory and may greatly improve our understanding of dark energy.

entries.title: New solid-state material converts sunlight into higher-energy UV light
entries.description: A new sunlight-powered material can convert visible light into higher-energy UV light, overcoming a challenge that has frustrated scientists for years. The breakthrough could enable cleaner air purification, solar-driven chemistry, and advanced manufacturing technologies using nothing more than natural sunlight.

entries.title: New superconducting X-ray detector is up to 1,000 times more sensitive
entries.description: A groundbreaking superconducting X-ray spectrometer has begun operation at BESSY II, giving Europe its first TES-based system and boosting photon detection efficiency by up to 1,000 times. The advance enables scientists to explore atomically thin materials, nanostructures, and ultra-dilute samples with remarkable speed and sensitivity.

entries.title: A portable ultrasound system could make reliable breast imaging more accessible
entries.description: The new technology, which generates high-resolution, 3D images of breast tissue, requires no expertise to operate and could be used at home.

entries.title: 390 gravitational wave detections reveal hidden population of black holes
entries.description: Astronomers have released the largest gravitational wave catalog ever, revealing 161 new black hole collisions and pushing the total number of detections to 390. Among the highlights are the clearest gravitational wave signal ever recorded, the most accurate location of a black hole merger, and growing evidence that some black holes are the products of previous black hole mergers. With discoveries now arriving several times a week, gravitational wave astronomy is entering an exciting new era.

entries.title: Colonialism was more than brutal force — it was an intellectual project
entries.description: A new book by UC Berkeley Professor Diego Pirillo argues that settler colonialism was shaped by Euro-American scholars, who worked hand in hand with land speculators and military leaders to drive the violent formation of the United States. entries.title: New fossils upend catastrophist narrative that flowering plants flourished only after dinosaur extinction
entries.description: Flowering plants, or angiosperms, now dominate Earth’s flora, but biologists thought they truly took off only after an asteroid impact 66 million years ago. A ‘botanical Pompeii’ containing fossilized seeds and fruits shows they prospered 10 million years earlier. The post New fossils upend catastrophist narrative that flowering plants flourished only after dinosaur extinction appeared first on Berkeley News.

entries.title: Scientists reveal what really happens when water is trapped in tiny spaces
entries.description: A decades-old puzzle about water has finally been unraveled. Researchers found that water trapped in tiny nanoscale spaces is not inherently more reactive. Instead, the intense pressures created inside these microscopic gaps explain most of the effect, while the surrounding material can further enhance water's chemistry if it interacts with the reaction products.

entries.title: Earth may have been seeding Venus with life for billions of years
entries.description: A new study suggests Earth may have been sending tiny hitchhikers to Venus for billions of years. Researchers found that asteroid impacts could launch microbes into space, where some might survive the journey and end up suspended in Venus' clouds. If future missions detect life there, there's a surprising chance it didn't originate on Venus at all—it may have come from Earth.

entries.title: How asteroids may have sparked life on Earth
entries.description: Ancient asteroid impacts may have done more than reshape Earth's surface—they could have helped spark life itself. New computer models show the collisions created enormous underground hydrothermal systems by cracking the planet's crust and allowing hot water to flow through it. These long-lasting, life-friendly environments may have covered much of the early Earth, turning cosmic destruction into an unexpected opportunity.
